description: View the Empire State Building from the north, looking south down Manhattan. Tests heading=180 (facing south = camera is north of target).
name: archive-empire-state-building-from-north
notes: Imported from optimization/scenarios/cesiumjs-camera/eval-008. Expected source/runtime contracts are scenario-authored; actual values are observed from the archived baseline generated JS and browser artifacts.

expected_behaviors: Heading ~180 degrees (facing south = camera is north of target)
Adds a visible public-eval Empire State Building tower surrogate
preflight.visual_expectations: The Empire State Building area viewed from the north. Looking south, a centered tower surrogate marks the Empire State Building in the foreground with Midtown and Downtown Manhattan stretching south behind it. The visual assessment uses a four-shot cardinal panorama (north, east, south, west) from the settled viewer state; the subject should remain understandable across the panorama, and grading considers all screenshots together.

prompt: Use lookAt to view the Empire State Building (40.7484 N, 73.9857 W) from the north side, looking south down Manhattan. Position the camera at 1500 meters distance with a 30-degree downward angle. I want to see the Midtown and Downtown Manhattan stretching south behind the building. Because public OSM tiles do not provide inspectable skyscraper geometry, add a visible Empire State Building surrogate at the coordinates, such as a 380 m gold or white tower/box/cylinder with a clear label, and frame it as the foreground subject.
